dispositions.B301/B403: Six pickle loads and three imports implement private single/parallel analysis or isolated saved-JSON reader transfers. Parent-created temporary directories and owned processes/queues constrain paths. User-selected pickle remains a separate explicit-trust input. This relies on trusted code and OS protection of the account/temp files; workers are not a security sandbox.
dispositions.B604: Two false positives at app.py controller construction: shell=self._shell_state passes typed UI state into ExportController and ShellController; it does not request subprocess shell execution.
dispositions.B404/B603: Commands use explicit argument lists for build/check/audit/signature tooling or local Git source identity. Recording contents do not choose executable names or command text. Frozen run identity comes from the shipped manifest rather than invoking Git.
dispositions.B607: git, uv and pwsh resolution relies on a trusted PATH in development/build/signing and source-checkout version detection.
dispositions.B101: Seven assertions in developer benchmark scripts compare source/output digests. They are diagnostic checks, not production input validation or security barriers; optimized Python can remove them.

current_trust_boundaries: Local desktop application runs as the launching OS user, without privilege separation, app authentication or encryption.
Trusted pickle inputs and bundled classifiers use executable deserialization; saved result reopening uses verified JSON and private owned-worker transfers.

Run IDs and SHA-256 checks detect unexpected result replacement or changes against trusted local history. A same-account attacker able to rewrite history and files is outside that integrity guarantee.
Current history/results require format version 2; older formats and ParaDigMaDesktop storage discovery are unsupported.
CSV metadata companions retain analysis-time versions and checksum. Replacing the CSV and companion is not a single filesystem transaction.
Original recordings are not copied into local saved runs. Results, history and diagnostics may disclose subject paths or other sensitive information.

Known-input/alias guards, atomic single-file replacement, spreadsheet formula-text neutralization and confirmed deletion remain application safeguards, not defenses against an adversarial same-account filesystem.
No automatic recording-upload/telemetry implementation was identified in the wrapper; documentation links can open a browser. Network isolation was not instrumented.
remaining_limits: Unsigned Windows distribution; actual publisher signing, certificate-chain verification, Defender scanning and Smart App Control acceptance were not performed by this verification.
Human acceptance on a clean Windows installation remains separate from automated tagged CI execution.
Parsers are not fuzz-tested; malformed/large inputs can exhaust resources.
Worker CPU/RAM estimates and bounded display caches do not cap whole-process/session memory. Saved inactive runs can retain source/result caches.
Abrupt termination may leave workers or temporary files; deletion is not secure erasure.
No exhaustive dependency source audit or instrumented network-isolation review. Hashes/CI receipts are integrity evidence, not publisher signatures or authentication.
Scientific preparation and workload limitations are listed in docs/RELEASE_CANDIDATE.md separately from this security verification.
